raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not chase fancy things. I farm the way that keeps the land steady and leaves some cash in my hand. On my 6.8 mu, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is our main food and cash pattern here, and I will keep a small piece in cotton because cotton still gives me another way to earn if grain price is not good. I have only two people at home, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I will put about 4.8 mu into wheat-maize double cropping and 2.0 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, use my usual local seed, put a good base fertilizer before sowing, then add a little more when the crop starts standing up strong in spring if the leaves look pale. I will irrigate a few times because our place depends on the well, but water costs money, so I will not water too often unless the soil is really dry.

For maize after wheat, I must move fast. After wheat harvest I will not do heavy tillage because there is no time. I will clear the straw, scratch the soil lightly, and sow maize within a few days. I will use hybrid maize seed because that is what gives a better ear, even though it costs more. I will not put too much fertilizer because I already spent on wheat, but I still need enough so the maize does not look weak in July. Cotton I will keep on the 2 mu where I usually plant it. Cotton needs more watching and more hand work, but on a small patch I can still manage. I will not spend too much on cotton fertilizer, because if I put too much money there, then I get tight on cash for wheat and maize. I will spray only when I really see insects or too many weeds.
